description: Experience the soul-warming depth of authentic Tonkotsu Ramen Broth, a culinary masterpiece born from hours of meticulous simmering. This creamy, opaque pork bone broth is the very foundation of a truly exceptional ramen bowl, offering an unparalleled richness and umami flavor that will transport your taste buds straight to Japan. Prepare to elevate your homemade ramen to professional standards with this traditional recipe.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pork Bones (Blanching)
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse the pork femurs and trotters under cold running water to remove any blood or impurities. Place the bones in a large stockpot, cover with cold water, and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Boil vigorously for 10-15 minutes, skimming off any scum that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Clean and Refresh Bones
instructions.text: Drain the blanched bones and rinse each piece thoroughly under cold water, scrubbing away any remaining dark impurities or coagulated blood. This step is crucial for a clear and clean-tasting broth. Clean the stockpot as well.

instructions.title: Initial Simmer with Aromatics
instructions.text: Return the cleaned bones to the clean stockpot. Add fresh cold water, ensuring the bones are fully submerged by at least 5-10 cm. Add the sliced ginger, smashed garlic, roughly chopped green onions, and quartered yellow onion. Bring the pot to a strong boil over high heat.

instructions.title: The Long Simmer (Emulsification)
instructions.text: Once boiling, reduce the heat slightly to maintain a vigorous, rolling boil. This high-heat simmer is essential for emulsifying the fat and collagen, creating the characteristic milky-white, creamy texture of Tonkotsu broth. Continue to simmer for 10-12 hours, adding hot water periodically to keep the bones submerged.

instructions.title: Skim and Maintain
instructions.text: Throughout the long simmering process, periodically skim off any excess foam or impurities that rise to the surface, especially during the first few hours. Stir the bones occasionally to prevent them from sticking to the bottom of the pot and to ensure even extraction of flavor. If using, add pork back fat during the last 4-6 hours of simmering for extra richness.

instructions.title: Strain the Broth
instructions.text: After 10-12 hours, the broth should be opaque and milky white, and the bones should be soft and brittle. Carefully remove all the bones and aromatics from the pot using tongs or a spider strainer. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean container to remove any small bone fragments or solids.

instructions.title: Final Adjustment and Cooling
instructions.text: Press any remaining solids in the sieve to extract maximum flavor. Allow the strained broth to cool slightly before refrigerating. The broth will thicken further as it cools. Skim any excess fat from the surface once chilled, if desired, before reheating and serving.

tips: For an exceptionally creamy broth, maintain a rolling boil throughout the entire cooking process. This high heat helps to emulsify the fats and collagen, creating the signature milky-white texture of Tonkotsu.
The blanching and thorough cleaning of the bones are critical steps. They prevent impurities from clouding your broth and ensure a clean, pure pork flavor without any off-notes.

Once the broth is fully cooked and strained, chill it completely. Any excess fat will solidify on top, making it easy to skim off if you prefer a less fatty broth. Store in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, or freeze for several months.
